title: An odd way to display leaderboards: You're an Ant on a huge Tree.
author: Vickie184
selftext:
This is a browser game/experience that came from me wanting a fun way to display the leaderboards from my other fishing/gathering browser game. You play as an Ant on a huge tree, where travelers have posted messages for various reasons. You, the player, can even leave a note that will last forever and age visually. Everyone sees everyone's notes, and it's multiplayer; you'll see other players as Ants, too. It also comes with a live Chat.

I create a larger, expansive world called Funkatron, in which this and all my other games/experiences are set in. The fishing/gathering game I mentioned has hundreds of unique fish and hundreds of unique resources you can gather and then pledge to your faction/city of choice. You can see the leaderboards in that game, of course, but also here on the big Tree. As my world grows, it's fun to come up with ways to tie it all together; This being one of them. 

I've written zero lines of code and spent zero time in blender. This all runs in a browser with no download and no install. Built in three.js, I've used GPT's Codex with Sol , Claude Code's Opus 5, Grok, Adobe After Effects, Suno, Gemini and MeshyAI for the 3d models.  


[https://tcpoole.com/notes/](https://tcpoole.com/notes/) to check it out. It's live and you might see other players there. Leave me a note! RP and write a note in character, add to the lore, or just say hello.   


I'll be hanging out in the game and here to answer any questions and explain in more detail.

comments.author: win-win-win-win_win
comments.body: Diegetic leaderboards are memorable, but I’d treat the tree as the discovery layer rather than the only scoreboard. The useful test is whether a returning player can answer two jobs quickly: “Where do I rank?” and “What changed since my last visit?” The tree could show spatial/status cues, then offer a compact fallback panel or a highlight trail from the ant to the relevant faction/name. That keeps the worldbuilding without making repeat checks expensive. I’d also watch whether permanent notes slowly bury the leaderboard signals—the content that makes the space feel alive can become information noise over time.

replies.author: Vickie184
replies.body: this is the most AI respone I've ever read. Wowza.

replies.author: win-win-win-win_win
replies.body: Fair. I over-structured it. Short version: the tree makes the leaderboard memorable, but returning players still need rank and change at a glance. That’s the tradeoff I meant.
